title: Include the passing boundary
objective: A score of 50 or higher passes. Change only the comparison in is_passing.
hints: Check what happens at exactly 50.
The boundary belongs to the passing group.
Use an inclusive greater-than comparison.
feedback: The >= comparison includes 50 as well as higher scores.

title: Accumulate every number
objective: total(numbers) must add all numbers. Correct the assignment inside the loop; keep the rest unchanged.
hints: Trace result after two different numbers.
The assignment replaces the previous total.
Add the current number to the existing result with +=.
feedback: += retains the accumulated sum instead of replacing it with the last number.

title: Avoid shared default state
objective: Each omitted items argument should get a new list. Use items=None and an if items is None initialization before append; keep other statements unchanged.
hints: Default argument objects are created once.
Use a sentinel to distinguish an omitted list.
Use None, then initialize [] inside an if items is None block.
feedback: The list is now created per call when the argument is omitted, while supplied lists remain usable.

title: Include the passing boundary
objective: isPassing(score) must return true for scores of 50 or higher. Change only > to the correct operator.
hints: Test the boundary score 50.
Equality must pass too.
Use >=.
feedback: The inclusive comparison accepts the boundary value.

title: Stop before the array ends
objective: total(numbers) must visit existing elements only. Change just the loop comparison.
starter_code: function total(numbers) { let sum = 0; for (let i = 0; i <= numbers.length; i++) { sum += numbers[i]; } return sum; }
solution: function total(numbers) { let sum = 0; for (let i = 0; i < numbers.length; i++) { sum += numbers[i]; } return sum; }
hints: Array indexes start at zero.
The last index is length minus one.
Use i < numbers.length.
feedback: The loop no longer visits numbers[length], which is outside the array.

title: Require a numeric zero
objective: isZero(value) should accept the number 0 but reject the string '0'. Change only the comparison operator.
hints: Loose equality can convert types.
The specification requires both type and value to match.
Use strict equality ===.
feedback: Strict equality compares without the coercion that would accept a string zero.

title: Connect a label to its field
objective: Connect the label to the input with id email. Change only the label's for attribute.
hints: Compare the label target and the input identifier.
The for attribute targets an element's id.
Set for to email.
feedback: The label now targets the email input by its identifier.

title: Keep Cancel from submitting
objective: Cancel must not submit this form. Change only the button type.
hints: The button is inside a form.
Its current type triggers submission.
Use type=button.
feedback: A button with type button has no default form-submit action.

title: Describe an informative image
objective: The image communicates 'Server offline'. Replace only the empty alt value with that exact description.
hints: This image carries information rather than decoration.
An empty alt attribute omits that information from its text alternative.
Set alt to Server offline.
feedback: The informative image now has the required text alternative. This checks the stated exercise, not accessibility of a whole page.

title: Target a class
objective: Target elements with class notice, not the id notice. Change only the selector.
hints: IDs and classes use different selector prefixes.
# selects an ID.
Use .notice.
feedback: The dot prefix selects a class.

title: Include padding in the width
objective: Keep padding within the declared width. Change only the box-sizing value.
hints: The content-box width excludes padding.
Choose the sizing mode that includes padding and borders.
Use border-box.
feedback: border-box includes padding and borders within the declared width.

title: Allow a class override
objective: The later .message rule should override the first rule for an element with id message and class message. Change only the first selector from an ID selector to the same class selector.
hints: An ID selector has greater specificity than a class selector.
Source order wins when specificity is equal.
Change #message to .message.
feedback: With equal specificity, the later rule sets blue under the exercise's stated conditions.
